correctness.rationale: Exact inverse of a general positive 2x2 matrix gives E=(y1-(b/d)y2,y2-(b/a)y1). Substitution into both ridge matrices produces a rank-one discrepancy with singular value D, attained at e2. Independent SymPy differentiation confirmed D prime numerator lambda-(1+3lambda)t²-t⁴ and the loss derivatives with factors t and lambda-t²; the unique stationary point and boundary-layer limit follow analytically. The inverse-multiquadric correlation t maps bijectively to positive shape parameter, whose derivative is strictly negative, preserving opposite gradient signs. No mistaken minimum is claimed.
residual_risks: Independent bounded arithmetic confirms key identities where noted; numerical tests do not substitute for the infinite/continuous proof.

originality.rationale: Lyu and Veiga introduce the same inverse-multiquadric Nyström/Rippa shape objective and discuss its numerical sensitivity, but the inspected full arXiv HTML does not derive the exact 2x2 rank-one residual operator, worst-case ridge divergence or the interval of opposite derivatives. Rippa gives the standard inverse-diagonal identity, not the matched-ridge comparison. Bucci–Nakatsukasa–Park investigate numerical Nyström stability, while this counterexample holds in exact arithmetic with core 1. The Rippa inverse-diagonal identity applies to both matrices but does not give their sharp difference or derivative sign for matched ridge; source shape numerical studies do not entail the exact classification.
residual_risks: Older Gaussian-process LOOCV or diagonal-correction literature might formulate an equivalent elementary two-site comparison.

value.rationale: Ridge-Nyström Rippa cross validation is specifically used to select kernel shape; exact sign disagreement between full and surrogate gradients is directly diagnostic of tuning failure. The exact two-site phase, attained worst-data amplification and small-ridge asymptotic constant constitute a sharp natural base case, not merely a numerical example.
residual_risks: The Nyström rank-one approximation is not spectrally accurate near the spike; well-conditioned full K does not imply small approximation error.
Spurious stationary point is a maximum, not a proven optimizer trap; higher-rank randomized prevalence unaddressed.

final_claim: For K_t=[[1,t],[t,1]], Q_t=[[1,t],[t,t²]], matched ridge 0<lambda<1 and inverse-diagonal leave-one-out residuals, the discrepancy operator norm equals D=t(1-t²)/((t²+lambda)(1+lambda)), uniquely optimized at t=sqrt(z_lambda) and sqrt(lambda) sup D ->1/2. For y=e2 the full squared loss is increasing in t and Nyström loss decreases for t>sqrt(lambda), with a spurious interior maximum at t=sqrt(lambda).
limitations: The Nyström rank-one approximation is not spectrally accurate near the spike; well-conditioned full K does not imply small approximation error.
Spurious stationary point is a maximum, not a proven optimizer trap; higher-rank randomized prevalence unaddressed.
